models.name: Airline fuel-cost shock
models.title: Airline fuel cost
models.covers: An airline's jet fuel bill (priced in US dollars, partly hedged) and the part of its change passed on to fares.
reasons: The knowledge graph states that Jet fuel price (U.S. Gulf Coast) affects costs of Air transport, the industry of Aerisca Airways. This decides whether the model applies, not how much: the amounts come from your figures.

issues.message: Rule T1 follows a relationship the knowledge graph records as a model assumption, not an empirical finding: results that depend on it are assumption-driven.

inputs.label: Crude oil price change
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Additional jet fuel price change
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Exchange-rate change
inputs.rationale: No change unless you enter one.

inputs.label: Crude-to-jet-fuel elasticity (β)
inputs.rationale: β = 1 keeps the refining margin a constant proportion of the price, so jet fuel moves by the same percentage as crude. A neutral starting point, not an estimate: test other values with sensitivity analysis.

inputs.label: Crude-to-jet-fuel lag
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes crude changes reach jet fuel in the same month. Set it to how the airline's fuel contracts reprice.

inputs.label: Hedge ratio
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes no hedging. Enter the share of the coming months' fuel the airline has hedged.

inputs.label: Hedge cover
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes no hedge cover. Hedges are assumed not to be rolled over when they expire.

inputs.label: Fare pass-through
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes fares do not change. Enter the share of a fuel-cost change the airline expects to pass on to passengers.

inputs.label: Fare pass-through lag
inputs.rationale: 0 assumes fares adjust in the same month as the fuel cost. Enter the delay you expect.

inputs.label: Horizon
inputs.rationale: Twelve months shows a full year after the shock.

inputs.label: Changes start in month
inputs.rationale: The changes take effect in the first month unless you set a later one.

inputs.label: Changes last for (months)
inputs.rationale: 0: the changes last for the rest of the horizon (a permanent step).

T1.description: A change in Brent crude reaches the jet fuel price with elasticity β after the stated lag.

S1.description: Jet fuel is a cost of air transport: the reason the fuel bill (E2–E10) belongs in an airline's operating costs. Cited, not propagated.

S2.description: The chosen airline operates in air transport.

S3.description: The exchange rate affects the chosen airline's costs (E3, E8). Cited, not propagated.

models.name: Floating-rate interest costs
models.title: Floating-rate interest
models.covers: Interest on floating-rate debt linked to the RBI repo rate or US short-term rates, after pass-through and repricing delays.
reasons: The knowledge graph does not state that RBI policy repo rate affects financing costs of or U.S. effective federal funds rate affects financing costs of Aerisca Airways or its industry.

issues.message: Aerisca Airways is a fictional company in RUMIN's sample network: the results describe the figures you entered, not a real company.
Rule T1 follows a relationship the knowledge graph records as a model assumption, not an empirical finding: results that depend on it are assumption-driven.
Floating-rate interest: the knowledge graph does not state this exposure of Aerisca Airways; the result rests on your figures alone.
Leave jet fuel out of the US-dollar costs: the airline fuel model already converts the fuel bill at the new exchange rate.

affected.note: Ties the knowledge graph states (assumptions or curated facts), not measured effects. A connection is not evidence of causation; only ties a model covers are simulated.
